description: 6 experimental setups for comparing VI, MC, and SARSA
note: Each experiment varies ONE factor while keeping others at tuned defaults

shaped.description: Base reward + bonus for moving closer to goal via BFS distance

unshaped.description: Base reward only, no BFS guidance

metrics.name: expected_return
metrics.description: Average cumulative reward over 20 greedy evaluation episodes
metrics.rationale: The fundamental RL objective — measures overall policy quality

metrics.name: policy_optimality_ratio
metrics.description: BFS shortest path / actual steps taken (0-1, 1=optimal)
metrics.rationale: Normalized policy quality metric, comparable across grids

metrics.name: convergence_speed
metrics.description: Episode/iteration at which policy stabilizes (95% success rate over window=50)
metrics.rationale: Measures sample efficiency — how quickly each algorithm learns

metrics.name: state_action_coverage
metrics.description: Fraction of reachable state-action pairs visited during training
metrics.rationale: Shows exploration behavior differences between on-policy (SARSA/MC) and model-based (VI)

experiments.name: Stochasticity: low noise
experiments.justification: Baseline comparison under near-deterministic conditions. All algorithms should perform well. Establishes reference performance.

experiments.name: Stochasticity: high noise
experiments.justification: Tests robustness to action noise. SARSA (on-policy) learns conservative paths accounting for noise. VI plans for deterministic model — policy may be brittle. MC suffers from high-variance episodes.

experiments.name: Discount factor: high (γ=0.95)
experiments.justification: High discount allows reward signal to propagate across the full 28-step path. All algorithms should converge to near-optimal policies.

experiments.name: Discount factor: low (γ=0.6)
experiments.justification: Low discount makes future rewards negligible after ~10 steps (0.6^28 ≈ 0.0003). Tests whether algorithms can still find the target. MC uses actual returns so may be less affected. VI/SARSA rely on bootstrapping discounted values.

experiments.name: Reward: without BFS shaping (baseline)
experiments.justification: No shaping — reward is sparse (+100 only at goal, -1 per step). Tests raw learning ability. VI unaffected (exact computation). SARSA/MC must discover goal through exploration alone.

experiments.name: Reward: with BFS shaping
experiments.justification: BFS shaping provides dense reward signal guiding agent toward goal. Tests how much shaping accelerates learning. Expected: convergence speed improves dramatically for SARSA/MC while VI sees little difference.
